findings.summary: restorePending trusts the pending record and does not check the current tree. It writes the saved bytes over each listed file (line 613) even when the file has changed since archive rewrote it, and it deletes the whole destination and stage folders with rmSync recursive (line 619) whenever the source exists. It also accepts any project path from the record for destination, stage and files[].path. Reproduced: a user note in docs/archive/x is deleted; a test edit after the interruption is lost; after git restore ., an edited archived copy is deleted; a later green archive of a sibling feature has its shared-test rewrite reverted; recovering two interrupted features in one order leaves a shared test naming a missing folder; a hand-edited destination "src" deletes src/ (receipts review-13-r2-user-edits.log, review-13-r2-two.log, review-13-r2-records.log lines 68-108). This breaks the rule that a record never causes data loss. Suggested fix: store the after-rewrite sha for each file and restore a file only when its current bytes still match that sha (or the before bytes); otherwise leave the file and report it. Require destination to be <archive home>/<folder> and stage to be a .<folder>.staging-* folder in the archive home, and require files[] to be listed files. Remove only the files archive wrote in the holder (archive-recovery.json, archive-replay.json, evidence, restored requirements, unverified.md); if anything else is there, move the feature back and report the extra files instead of deleting them.

archiveFeature calls resolveFolder before recoverPending. If the process dies between renameSync(source, stage/feature) and renameSync(stage, destination), the feature is only in docs/archive/.x.staging-*, which resolveFolder skips (dot-folder), so every later call exits 1 with "No feature folder for x" and never reads the pending record that holds the stage path (receipt review-13-r2-stages.log lines 56-109). Nothing is lost and nothing reports archived, but the next call does not restore. The window is two adjacent sync calls. Suggested fix: look for archive-pending/<name>.json (and dated matches) before resolveFolder, or let resolveFolder fall back to a pending record.

A truncated record stops every archive call with "Invalid JSON: .joycraft/local/archive-pending/x.json" while the folder stays at docs/archive/x and the tests stay rewritten (receipt review-13-r2-records.log lines 1-44). No data is lost, but the message does not say how to recover (for example: git restore the listed files, move docs/archive/x/feature back, delete the record).
findings.assumption: A corrupt record is rare; a plain recovery hint is enough.
